_meta.name: Smart Agriculture Copilot - Fertilizer & Regional Soil Knowledge Base
_meta.purpose: Ground truth for the AI advisor: maps region -> soil type -> well-known fertilizers/amendments -> crop-wise nutrient doses. The AI must answer only from this file plus live weather/soil-moisture data and any soil-test values the farmer provides.

units.area: Doses are stored per hectare (ha). 1 ha = 2.471 acre. Bigha size differs by state, so ask the farmer or use a local conversion.
units.nutrients: N = nitrogen, P2O5 = phosphate, K2O = potash, S = sulphur, Zn = zinc, B = boron. Doses are NUTRIENT kg, not fertilizer kg.

confidence_legend.high: Cross-checked against ICAR / ICAR-journal / government-institute sources during compilation.
confidence_legend.medium: Standard state agricultural university package-of-practices style ranges; not individually re-verified. Treat as indicative.

_meta.disclaimer: Indicative guidance only. Real doses depend on a soil test (Soil Health Card), crop variety, irrigation, yield target and state recommendations. Always advise the farmer to confirm with the local KVK / agriculture department. Brand names are examples of widely available products, not endorsements; availability varies by state and season.
sources: https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4174/3849 (Site-specific NPK in wheat, Indian J. Agronomy)

ai_usage_rules: Identify the farmer's location (state/district) and map it to a soil type using region_hints. If the farmer names their soil in local words (kaali mitti, lal mitti, ooshar/reh, retili mitti) use soil_types[].name_hi. If a soil test or Soil Health Card value is available, it overrides the regional typical values.
Before recommending, make sure you know: crop, season (kharif/rabi/zaid), irrigated or rainfed, land area, and whether a soil test exists. Ask for what is missing - one question at a time.
Recommend only fertilizers listed in this file. Use common names (Urea, DAP, MOP, SSP, NPK 12:32:16, etc.). Brands may be mentioned as examples of commonly available products.
Always convert nutrient doses into fertilizer kg and bags using the conversion rules, and express them per acre (and per bigha only if the farmer gives the local bigha size).
Always give timing (basal vs top-dress) and one cost-saving tip. For farmers with limited resources use the low_resource_playbook.

Protect the soil: never advise more than the maximum of the crop range. Prefer split nitrogen, add organic matter on light soils, and use gypsum/zinc/sulphur only where the soil type or soil test indicates a need.
Nano fertilizers: advise them as a partial replacement of top-dressed urea only. Do not tell farmers to drop the basal dose. Mention that field results vary.
Never give pesticide or herbicide doses. For safety remind: wear gloves/mask when spraying or handling, keep fertilizers away from children, do not spray in wind or just before rain.
Never promise yield increases. Say 'can help' and refer to the local KVK / agriculture officer for a soil test.
Answer in the farmer's language (Hindi/English/regional) in short, simple sentences. Use bags and acres, not scientific terms.
answer_template: 2) What to apply for <crop>: fertilizer name -> kg per acre -> bags
4) Soil fix needed? (zinc, gypsum, lime, organic manure) - only if relevant
5) Low-cost option if resources are limited
6) One caution + suggestion to confirm with soil test / KVK

conversion_rules.ha_to_acre: divide kg/ha by 2.471 to get kg/acre
order_of_calculation: 1. Fix the P2O5 dose first using DAP (or SSP / NPK complex).
2. Subtract the nitrogen supplied by DAP (DAP kg x 0.18) from the total N dose.
3. Supply the remaining N from Urea.
4. Supply K2O from MOP (or SOP for chloride-sensitive crops).
5. Add S, Zn, B only where indicated.

fertilizers.name: Urea
fertilizers.role: Main nitrogen source for cereals, sugarcane, vegetables. Urea sold in India is neem-coated.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Top-dress in 2-3 splits on moist soil; do not apply on standing water or just before heavy rain.
cautions: Large nitrogen losses (ammonia) on alkaline/sodic soils and when broadcast on dry hot soil.
Over-use gives soft, lodging-prone plants and pest attack; do not exceed crop dose.

fertilizers.name: DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate)
fertilizers.role: Basal phosphorus plus starter nitrogen. Second most used fertilizer in India after urea.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal, placed in the seed furrow below/beside the seed (seed drill) or broadcast and mixed before sowing.
cautions: Do not let DAP touch the seed directly (ammonia burn).
On black and calcareous soils phosphorus gets fixed - place it near roots rather than broadcasting.

fertilizers.name: MOP (Muriate of Potash)
fertilizers.role: Potassium for potato, sugarcane, vegetables, fruits, and for rice-wheat fields where potassium is being mined.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal, mixed in soil. For sandy soils split half basal, half at top-dressing.
cautions: Contains chloride - for chloride-sensitive crops (tobacco, grapes, quality potato) and saline soils prefer SOP.
Black soils are usually high in potassium - apply only if soil test shows low K.

fertilizers.name: SSP (Single Super Phosphate)
fertilizers.role: Phosphorus plus sulphur and calcium. Best for oilseeds (mustard, groundnut, soybean), pulses and sulphur-deficient soils.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal. Does not supply nitrogen, so pair with urea.
cautions: Bulkier than DAP - more bags needed per kg of P2O5.

fertilizers.name: NPK 10:26:26
fertilizers.role: High phosphorus + potassium. Used basal for potato, cotton, groundnut, pulses, vegetables and for root/flower development.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal; top up nitrogen with urea.
cautions: Check that total P2O5 and K2O supplied do not exceed the crop range.

fertilizers.name: NPK 12:32:16
fertilizers.role: High phosphorus grade for good early root growth and flowering - cereals, pulses, oilseeds, vegetables.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal; top up nitrogen with urea.
cautions: On potassium-rich black soils there may be no need for the extra K.

fertilizers.name: NPK 15:15:15 (balanced)
fertilizers.role: All-purpose balanced fertilizer for vegetables, fruits and general crops.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal or at early growth stage.
cautions: Lower nutrient density; costs more per kg of nutrient than straight fertilizers.

fertilizers.name: NPS 20:20:0:13 (Ammonium Phosphate Sulphate)
fertilizers.role: Nitrogen + phosphorus + sulphur in one bag. Good for mustard, soybean, groundnut, pulses and sulphur-deficient fields.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal.
cautions: No potassium - add MOP where potash is needed.

fertilizers.name: NPK 19:19:19 (water soluble)
fertilizers.role: For drip/fertigation and foliar sprays in vegetables, fruits, flowers - quick correction during stress.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Fertigation or foliar spray at label rate (commonly about 0.5%, i.e. 5 g per litre for foliar).
cautions: Costly for field crops; use only for high-value crops or as a stress-recovery spray.

fertilizers.name: Ammonium Sulphate
fertilizers.role: Nitrogen + sulphur. Preferred over urea on alkaline/sodic soils and for rice, mustard, onion on sulphur-poor soils.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal or top-dress in splits.
cautions: Acidifies soil - avoid repeated heavy use on acidic soils (red/laterite/hill).

fertilizers.name: SOP (Sulphate of Potash)
fertilizers.role: Chloride-free potassium + sulphur for potato quality, fruits, vegetables, tobacco and saline soils.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Basal.
cautions: More expensive than MOP - use mainly where chloride is a problem.

fertilizers.name: Zinc Sulphate

nutrient_percent.note: 21% as heptahydrate; 33% as monohydrate - check the bag

fertilizers.role: Corrects zinc deficiency, which is widespread in Indian soils - important for rice, wheat, maize, sodic and calcareous soils.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Soil: about 25 kg/ha (21% grade) once, usually before rice; residual effect lasts into the next crop. Foliar: 0.5% solution (5 g per litre) with 0.25% lime at deficiency symptoms.
cautions: Do not mix directly with phosphate fertilizers before application; mix with dry soil/sand and broadcast.
Do not overdose - repeat only on soil-test or symptom evidence.

fertilizers.name: Borax / Boron
fertilizers.role: Boron for flowering and pod/fruit set; deficient in calcareous alluvium (Bihar, eastern UP), red/laterite soils; important for mustard, potato, vegetables, cauliflower, groundnut.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Soil: about 5-10 kg borax/ha on deficient soils. Foliar: very dilute (about 0.1-0.2%).
cautions: Safe range is narrow - boron overdose is toxic. Use only where deficiency is known or visible.

fertilizers.name: Gypsum
fertilizers.role: (a) Sulphur and calcium source for oilseeds, pulses and groundnut; (b) main amendment for reclaiming sodic (ooshar/reh) soils.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Sulphur use: about 200-250 kg/ha for oilseeds/pulses. Groundnut: about 250-500 kg/ha at pegging/flowering. Sodic reclamation: dose from soil test as 'gypsum requirement (GR)' - common practice 50% of GR; research supports 25% of GR with organic manure/pressmud and salt-tolerant varieties.
cautions: For sodic soils always test first; incorporate and irrigate/leach with good-quality water.
Not a substitute for lime on strongly acidic soils.

fertilizers.name: Pyrite (iron pyrite)
fertilizers.role: Amendment for CALCAREOUS sodic soils (e.g., parts of Bihar), where it can work better than gypsum alone.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Dose from soil test via KVK/soil lab; incorporate in surface soil.
cautions: Needs oxidation in the soil; use only on advice from soil lab / agriculture university.

fertilizers.name: Agricultural Lime / Dolomite
fertilizers.role: Raises pH of acidic soils (laterite, red, hill/forest, acid Assam/Kerala soils); frees phosphorus; dolomite also corrects magnesium deficiency.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Dose follows the soil's lime requirement (indicative 2-5 t/ha on strongly acid soils; split over years). Apply 2-3 weeks before sowing and mix into soil. Target pH about 6-6.5.
cautions: Do not apply on neutral/alkaline soils.
Do not apply on the same day as urea/ammonium fertilizers.
known_brands: Dolomite / agricultural lime from local suppliers (state agriculture department)

fertilizers.name: Farmyard Manure (FYM) / Compost

nutrient_percent.note: low and variable nutrient content; main value is organic matter, water holding and microbial life

fertilizers.role: Rebuilds soil organic carbon; essential on red, laterite, light/sandy and arid soils and in rice-wheat fields.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Well-decomposed, about 5-10 t/ha (2-4 t/acre) mixed into soil 2-3 weeks before sowing. Can reduce chemical fertilizer need over time.
cautions: Use only well-decomposed manure (fresh manure can burn seedlings and bring weeds/termites).

fertilizers.name: Vermicompost

nutrient_percent.note: nutrient-rich compost; use smaller quantity than FYM

fertilizers.role: Concentrated organic manure for vegetables, fruits and nursery beds.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: About 2-5 t/ha (1-2 t/acre) mixed in soil at sowing/planting.

fertilizers.name: Pressmud (sugar-mill by-product)

nutrient_percent.note: organic matter, some P and Ca

fertilizers.role: Used with gypsum to cut the cost of sodic soil reclamation; useful near sugar-mill regions.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: About 10 t/ha along with reduced gypsum (e.g., Bihar calcareous sodic trials).
cautions: Use decomposed pressmud.

fertilizers.name: Biofertilizers (Rhizobium, PSB, Azotobacter/Azospirillum, KMB)
fertilizers.role: Rhizobium for pulses/soybean/groundnut (fixes nitrogen); PSB makes soil phosphorus available; Azotobacter/Azospirillum for cereals and vegetables.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Seed treatment before sowing - follow the dose printed on the packet; dry in shade.
cautions: Check expiry date; do not mix with chemical seed treatment at the same time (treat fungicide first, dry, then biofertilizer).
known_brands: State agriculture university / KVK biofertilizer packets

fertilizers.name: Green manure (Dhaincha / Sunhemp)
fertilizers.role: Adds nitrogen and organic matter before rice; helps in sodic soil reclamation.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Sow before the season and plough in at about 45-50 days (flowering).
cautions: Needs 6-8 weeks of field time before the main crop.

fertilizers.name: Nano Urea (liquid) / Nano Urea Plus

nutrient_percent.note: Nano Urea = 4% N (w/v); Nano Urea Plus = 20% N (w/v)

fertilizers.role: Foliar nitrogen spray. One 500 ml bottle is positioned as equivalent to one 45 kg bag of urea. Reduces part of the top-dressed urea.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Mix 2-4 ml per litre of water and spray on leaves. Usually 2 sprays: 1st at active tillering/branching (30-35 days after germination or 20-25 days after transplanting), 2nd about 20-25 days later or before flowering. Typical volume 250-500 ml product per acre. Spray in morning/evening, avoid dew; repeat if rain falls within 12 hours.
cautions: Do NOT cut the basal nitrogen from DAP/complex fertilizers - cut only part of the top-dress urea.
Some trials (e.g., Punjab wheat) reported lower yield when nano urea replaced the full urea dose - advise partial replacement.
Foliar only - not for soil application.
known_brands: Nano Urea (liquid) from NFL / RCF under licence

fertilizers.name: Nano DAP (liquid)
fertilizers.role: Liquid N + P for seed treatment and foliar spray; can reduce part of the conventional DAP dose.
fertilizers.how_to_apply: Foliar: about 250-500 ml per acre per spray in water at critical stages. Seed/root treatment as per label.
cautions: Use as a supplement; do not skip the basal phosphorus on P-deficient soils unless a soil test supports it.

soil_types.name: Alluvial soil
regions: Deltas of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu
sub_types: Khadar - newer floodplain alluvium, more fertile
Bhangar - older alluvium, more kankar/lime nodules, less fertile
soil_types.typical_ph: 6.5-8.5 (neutral to alkaline; calcareous in parts of Bihar, eastern UP, Haryana)
soil_types.texture_and_water: Loam to sandy loam to clay loam; medium water holding; good drainage

nutrient_status.iron: adequate; deficiency in high-pH calcareous patches

main_problems: Zinc and sulphur deficiency in rice-wheat belt
Sodic (ooshar/usar) and saline patches in UP, Punjab, Haryana
strategy: Balanced N-P-K with N in 2-3 splits
Add zinc sulphate before rice (once in 2-3 seasons if deficient)
Add sulphur (SSP/gypsum/NPS) for mustard, pulses
Return crop residue / FYM / green manure to rebuild organic carbon

recommended_fertilizers.role: Potash for potato, sugarcane and long-running rice-wheat fields
P + sulphur for mustard, pulses, vegetables
N + P + S basal for oilseeds/pulses
Sulphur source; reclamation where sodic patches exist
Replace part of top-dress urea to cut cost/losses

avoid_or_caution: Urea broadcast on dry soil or before heavy rain (N loss)
Heavy chloride (MOP) for chloride-sensitive potato quality

soil_types.name: Black soil (Regur / black cotton soil)
soil_types.texture_and_water: Heavy clay; very high water holding; swells when wet, cracks when dry; poor drainage/waterlogging risk
main_problems: Low N, P and organic matter
Waterlogging in heavy rain; hard to work when wet or dry
strategy: Place phosphorus near the roots (seed drill) instead of broadcasting
Split nitrogen; avoid heavy doses before heavy rain
Skip or reduce potash unless soil test is low
Apply zinc sulphate and sulphur (SSP/gypsum) for cotton, soybean, oilseeds

recommended_fertilizers.role: Basal P placed in seed furrow
P + S for soybean, groundnut, pulses
N + P + S for soybean/cotton basal
Zinc for cotton, soybean, sorghum, wheat

avoid_or_caution: Routine heavy MOP (potassium is usually adequate)

soil_types.name: Red (and yellow) soil
soil_types.texture_and_water: Light to medium, gravelly/sandy loam; low water holding; drains fast; low CEC
main_problems: Low organic matter and water holding
strategy: Add FYM/compost every year
Use more but smaller N and K splits (light soil leaches)
Lime if pH below about 5.5
Prefer SSP/NPS for P + S; add zinc and boron where deficient

recommended_fertilizers.role: First priority - builds water holding and nutrient retention
P + S + Ca; good on acidic red soils
Potash split half basal, half top-dress
Boron where symptoms/soil test show deficiency
Only if soil is acidic (pH below about 5.5)

avoid_or_caution: Single heavy dose of urea or MOP (leaches away)
Repeated ammonium sulphate on acidic patches

soil_types.name: Laterite soil
soil_types.texture_and_water: Gravelly/sandy clay loam; heavy leaching in high rainfall; low CEC
main_problems: Aluminium/iron toxicity at very low pH
strategy: Lime first (per soil test), then fertilize
Use SSP/NPS rather than relying on DAP alone
Heavy organic manure and mulch
Split N and K in small doses

recommended_fertilizers.role: Correct acidity (dolomite if Mg is also low)

avoid_or_caution: Ammonium sulphate as the only N source (acidifies further)

soil_types.name: Arid / desert soil
regions: South-west Haryana and Punjab (Bhiwani, Mahendragarh, Sirsa fringe)
soil_types.texture_and_water: Sandy; very low water holding; wind erosion; salinity in patches
main_problems: Water scarcity - rainfed dose must be lower
Fertilizer burn risk when moisture is low
strategy: Match dose to rainfall/irrigation - rainfed crops need low N-P with good manure
Use FYM/compost and mulching
Prefer drip + fertigation where water exists
Sulphur for mustard; zinc/iron where deficient

recommended_fertilizers.role: Low rainfed doses, apply when soil is moist
P + S for mustard, pulses, bajra
Sulphur for oilseeds; sodic patches (after soil test)
Foliar N saves soil-applied urea in dry spells

avoid_or_caution: Heavy urea doses in dry soil (burn and loss)
Chloride-heavy fertilizers in saline patches - prefer SOP

soil_types.name: Mountain / forest soil
regions: High ranges of the Western Ghats
soil_types.texture_and_water: Variable, shallow on slopes; high organic matter in forest soils; erosion risk

nutrient_status.organic_carbon: high in forest areas, low on eroded slopes

main_problems: Erosion and nutrient loss on slopes
strategy: Terracing and mulching plus balanced fertilizer
Lime on very acidic fields
Apply boron to apple/vegetables where deficient

recommended_fertilizers.role: P + S + Ca for acidic hill soils

avoid_or_caution: Broadcasting fertilizer on steep slopes before rain (runoff)

soil_types.name: Saline / sodic (alkali) soil
regions: Uttar Pradesh (usar lands, e.g. Raebareli, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Unnao belts)
sub_types: Sodic/alkali (pH above 8.5, often 9-10.5, poor drainage, white crust)
soil_types.typical_ph: 8.5-10.5 for sodic; saline soils may be near neutral but high in salts
soil_types.texture_and_water: Dense, hard when dry, sticky when wet; very low permeability when sodic

nutrient_status.phosphorus: often adequate (Olsen-P can be high in sodic soils)

reclamation_protocol: 1. Test the soil (pH, EC, ESP) at a soil lab / KVK - gypsum requirement (GR) is calculated from it.

2. Apply gypsum (common practice 50% of GR; research supports 25% of GR combined with pressmud/FYM/green manure and salt-tolerant varieties). Calcareous sodic: consider pyrite or gypsum plus organics on advice.
3. Mix in surface soil, level, bund and leach with good-quality water.
4. First crops: green manure (dhaincha) or salt-tolerant rice; later wheat/mustard.
6. Use ammonium sulphate or split urea; hold back phosphorus where soil-test P is already high.

recommended_fertilizers.role: Core amendment (dose from soil-test gypsum requirement)
Cheapens reclamation when used with reduced gypsum
Better N source than urea on alkaline soil
Only in more split doses; high loss otherwise
If potash needed, avoid chloride in saline soil

avoid_or_caution: Leaching saline-sodic soil with water but no gypsum (makes it more sodic)
Heavy DAP/phosphorus where Olsen-P is already high

region_hints.zone: Western plains (Gautam Buddh Nagar, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Bulandshahr, Muzaffarnagar, Saharanpur)
region_hints.notes: Loam/sandy-loam alluvium; wheat-sugarcane-rice belt; watch potassium, zinc and sulphur; occasional sodic patches.

region_hints.zone: Central and eastern plains (Lucknow, Raebareli, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Unnao, Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Ayodhya)
region_hints.notes: Alluvium with well-known usar/sodic belts in Raebareli, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Unnao; reclamation with gypsum widely practised.

region_hints.zone: Bundelkhand (Jhansi, Banda, Hamirpur, Chitrakoot, Lalitpur, Jalaun, Mahoba)
region_hints.notes: Mixed red and black soils, rainfed and water-scarce; lower rainfed doses plus organic manure.

region_hints.zone: Terai belt (Pilibhit, Lakhimpur Kheri, Bahraich, Shravasti, Balrampur)
region_hints.notes: Moist, heavier alluvium with higher organic matter; rice-wheat-sugarcane.
Loamy to sandy alluvium; zinc deficiency in rice, manganese in wheat after rice on sandy soils; south-west has saline/sodic patches.
Sodic belt near Karnal-Kaithal-Kurukshetra; sandy arid soils in Bhiwani and Mahendragarh.
Calcareous alluvium (e.g. Samastipur, Muzaffarpur): zinc, sulphur and boron deficiency common; calcareous sodic patches.

region_hints.zone: Gangetic delta, coast and western plateau
region_hints.notes: Delta alluvium for rice/jute; coastal saline in Sundarbans; laterite in Bankura/Purulia/Birbhum.
Acidic soils; low-input rice doses are common (e.g. about 60:20:40 NPK for Sali rice) and lime helps.

region_hints.zone: Deccan plateau (Vidarbha, Marathwada, western Maharashtra) and Konkan
region_hints.notes: Black soils for cotton, soybean, sugarcane, onion; Konkan laterite is acidic.

region_hints.zone: Malwa and Narmada valley; eastern MP
region_hints.notes: Soybean-wheat-chickpea on black soils; eastern districts have red and yellow soils.

region_hints.zone: Saurashtra, south, central-north, Kutch and coast
region_hints.notes: Cotton/groundnut on black and medium black; saline coastal and Kutch soils.
Mustard, bajra, guar in arid zone; Hadoti (Kota-Baran-Jhalawar) has black soils.
Ragi/groundnut on red soils; cotton/jowar/pulses on black soils in the north; acidic laterite near the coast.
Delta alluvium for rice; red soils widespread; black soils in western and southern belts.
Deltaic alluvium for rice; black cotton soils in Guntur/Krishna; red soils in Rayalaseema.
Red chalka and black regur soils; cotton, rice, maize, soybean.
Coastal deltaic alluvium; acidic red/laterite uplands.
Red and yellow soils, acidic in places; rice-based systems - lime and organic manure help.
Strongly acidic laterite; lime and organic manure are the first step.
Acidic hill soils for apple, potato, vegetables; Terai/valley areas are alluvial.

crops.name: Wheat
extras: Sulphur about 20-30 kg S/ha on S-deficient soils (SSP/gypsum/NPS)
crops.split_schedule: Half N + all P and K at sowing; rest N at first irrigation (crown root initiation, 20-25 days) and second at tillering/second irrigation.
crops.notes: 150:60:40 is the commonly recommended dose for irrigated timely-sown wheat; late sowing: use the lower N (about 100-120). Site-specific trials in eastern UP found higher potash (up to 60-120 K2O) paid on K-poor soils - go by soil test.

crops.name: Rice (paddy)
extras: Zinc sulphate 25 kg/ha before transplanting in zinc-deficient soils
Green manure (dhaincha) can save part of the N
Low-input lowland (Assam Sali) can use about 60:20:40 - follow state recommendation
crops.split_schedule: N in 3 splits: one-third basal, one-third at active tillering, one-third at panicle initiation. All P and K basal.
crops.notes: Basmati usually needs less N (about 100-120). Hybrid boro rice in Assam is recommended about 100:60:60.

crops.name: Maize
extras: Zinc sulphate 25 kg/ha on zinc-deficient soils
crops.split_schedule: N in 3 splits: basal, knee-high stage, pre-tasselling. P and K basal.
crops.notes: Soil-test based 120:60:40 is a standard recommendation for maize-wheat systems.

crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.split_schedule: N in 2-3 splits during early growth/tillering; avoid late N. Ratoon crops need more N than plant crop.
crops.notes: Follow the state sugarcane department / mill-zone recommendation which varies by state.

crops.name: Mustard / rapeseed
extras: Sulphur 30-40 kg S/ha is crucial (use SSP, NPS, ammonium sulphate or gypsum)
crops.split_schedule: Half N + all P, K and S at sowing; rest N at first irrigation (about 25-30 days).
crops.notes: Rainfed mustard needs only about 40:20:0 plus sulphur.

crops.name: Potato
crops.split_schedule: Half N + all P and K at planting; remaining N at earthing-up (25-30 days).
crops.notes: High potash improves tuber size and storage.

crops.name: Chickpea (gram)
extras: Sulphur 20 kg S/ha on S-poor soils

crops.name: Field pea / garden pea
crops.notes: Garden pea for vegetable uses the higher P and K.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.notes: Responds strongly to phosphorus and sulphur.

crops.name: Cotton (irrigated Bt hybrid)
extras: Zinc and magnesium on deficient soils
Water-soluble NPK through drip where available
crops.split_schedule: N in 3-4 splits (sowing, square formation, flowering, boll development); P at sowing; K split.
crops.notes: Rainfed cotton on black soils needs lower doses - follow state recommendation.

crops.name: Groundnut
extras: Gypsum 250-500 kg/ha at pegging/flowering for calcium and sulphur
crops.notes: Light red/sandy soils respond to potash and gypsum.

crops.name: Pearl millet (bajra)
crops.split_schedule: Half N + all P basal; rest N at about 30 days when soil is moist.
crops.notes: Use the lower dose for rainfed fields and the higher for irrigated hybrids.

crops.name: Sorghum (jowar)
extras: Zinc/iron on black soils if deficient
crops.split_schedule: Half N + P at sowing; rest N at 30-35 days.
crops.notes: Rainfed about 40:20:0; irrigated hybrid up to 80-100 N.

crops.name: Tomato
extras: Calcium and boron for fruit set / blossom-end rot
crops.split_schedule: Basal P, K and part N; remaining N in 3-4 splits at 20-day gaps; more potash at fruiting.
crops.notes: Even moisture reduces blossom-end rot and cracking.

crops.name: Onion
extras: Sulphur 30-40 kg S/ha (improves pungency and storage)
crops.split_schedule: Half N + all P and K basal; remaining N in two splits up to about 45 days; no N after bulb initiation.
crops.notes: Late N makes bulbs store poorly.

low_resource_playbook.idea: When money, water or inputs are limited, protect yield per rupee instead of chasing maximum yield.
priority_order: 1. Get a soil test / Soil Health Card (often free) - it removes guesswork and saves fertilizer.
2. Fix the cheapest big limiter first: zinc sulphate (cheap, big response in rice/wheat/maize) and sulphur (SSP/gypsum) for oilseeds and pulses.
3. Put phosphorus in the seed furrow (placement) instead of broadcasting - same crop with less DAP.
4. Split urea in 2-3 small doses on moist soil; avoid applying before heavy rain.
5. Add FYM/compost, crop residue or green manure (dhaincha) to cut fertilizer need over time.
6. Use legumes in rotation with Rhizobium/PSB seed treatment (nitrogen from air).
7. Consider Nano Urea sprays to replace part of the top-dress urea - never the basal dose.
8. Match the dose to water: rainfed fields need lower N and P; do not apply the irrigated dose without irrigation.
low_resource_playbook.crop_choice_hint: In dry or low-input conditions prefer lower-nutrient crops (bajra, sorghum, pulses, mustard, chickpea) and legumes; compare expected profit using current mandi prices before suggesting a crop.
